name: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context
problem: Single-device attention cannot exceed a fixed sequence length on available HBM, and simply spilling sequences to many devices either breaks training parallelism or pays for communication.
mechanism: Blockwise self-attention and feedforward computation are distributed across devices so that each device owns a contiguous subsequence, while the communication of key-value blocks is FULLY OVERLAPPED with the computation of blockwise attention on the ring of devices. Overlap is achieved by interleaving per-block compute and per-block communication, so the collective is hidden behind useful work.
speedup_reported: NO SPEEDUP NUMBER IN THE ABSTRACT. The claim is about REACH rather than rate: enables training and inference of sequences up to DEVICE-COUNT TIMES longer than prior memory-efficient Transformers, without approximation and without additional communication or computation overheads, demonstrated at millions of tokens and improving performance on language modelling and RL. The zero-overhead property is the claim worth carrying.
